Rashi on Shabbat 145a:11:1.hebrew: סוחטין כבשין - ולא מפליג בין לגופן בין למימיהן, ושרי לכתחילה, וקשיא לכולהו, דליכא בהו דשרי כבשין למימיהן לכתחילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:11:1.english: One may squeeze pickled vegetables - And [the baraita] does not distinguish between [squeezing them] for their own [consumption] and for their juice, and permits [it] ab initio; and [thus] it is difficult for all of them, for there is none among them who permits [squeezing] pickled vegetables for their juice ab initio.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:15:1.hebrew: דבר תורה - כלומר, אסרה תורה מלאכה, ודריכת זיתים וענבים הוא דהויא מלאכה; אבל שאר דריכות לאו אורחייהו בהכי, ולאו מלאכה נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:15:1.english: By Torah law - That is to say, the Torah prohibited labor, and [specifically] the treading of olives and grapes is what constitutes labor; however, other treadings are not their normal way [of processing], and they are not [considered] labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:1:1.hebrew: טמא מת שסחט זיתים וענבים כביצה מכוונת טהור - משנה היא במסכת טהרות, ומפרש בה בהדיא: "ובלבד שלא יגע במשקה", שאינו נוגע אלא באוכל. וכיון דכביצה מכוונת הוא, לכי סחיט טיפה קמייתא חסר ליה מכביצה, ואין האוכל — אע"פ שהוא טמא — מטמא המשקה, שאין אוכל מטמא אחרים בפחות מכביצה. אבל אם היה נוגע במשקה, איטמי ליה משקה מטיפה ראשונה, שהמשקה מקבל טומאה בכל שהוא. וה"נ תני בה בהדיא: "יותר מכביצה — טמא", שכיון שיצאה טיפה ראשונה נטמאה בכביצה. וטמא מת דווקא נקט, שאינו מטמא בהיסט, וה"ה לטמא שרץ וכל טמאי מגע. וטמא מת לרבותא נקט, דהוי אב הטומאה, משום דקתני סיפא: "אבל זב שסוחט זיתים וענבים, אפי' גרגיר יחידי — טמא", שכיון שיצאה טיפה ראשונה נטמא המשקה במשא הזב:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:1:1.english: One who is ritually impure from a corpse who squeezed olives and grapes [in the amount of] an exact egg-bulk, [it is] ritually pure - It is a Mishnah in Tractate Taharot, and it explicitly states therein: "provided that he does not touch the liquid" — for he touches only the food. And since it is an exact egg-bulk, when he squeezes out the first drop, it becomes less than an egg-bulk, and the food — even though it is impure — does not render the liquid impure, for food does not render other things impure when it is less than an egg-bulk. However, if he were touching the liquid, the liquid would become impure from the first drop, because liquid contracts impurity in any amount. And so too is it explicitly taught therein: "more than an egg-bulk — [it is] impure," for once the first drop emerges, it becomes impure through the [remaining] egg-bulk. And [the Mishnah] specifically mentioned one who is impure from a corpse, because he does not impart impurity by moving [an object], and the same law applies to one impure from a creeping creature and all those who impart impurity by contact. And it mentioned one impure from a corpse to teach the greater extent, for he is a primary source of impurity — because the latter clause teaches: "but a zav who squeezes olives and grapes, even a single berry — [it is] impure," for once the first drop emerges, the liquid becomes impure through being carried by the zav.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:1:2.hebrew: ואי אמרת כו' - דקס"ד אפי' סוחט לתוך הקדירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:1:2.english: And if you say, etc. - For it was initially assumed [that this applies] even [to one who] squeezes into the pot.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:1.hebrew: כתנאי - משקה הבא לאוכל, אוכל הוא או משקה הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:1.english: [It is] like [a dispute between] Tannaim - Is a liquid that comes into food food, or is it a liquid?

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:2.hebrew: המחליק בענבים - נחתום המחליק פני ככרותיו בענבים, שסוחט המשקה על הככר:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:2.english: One who smooths with grapes - A baker who smooths the surface of his loaves with grapes, [in] that he squeezes the liquid onto the loaf.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:3.english: It was rendered susceptible - The food, [namely] the grapes, were rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity].

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:4.hebrew: הבא - לצורך אוכל, כגון שסחטן לשם הפת:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:2:4.english: That comes - For the need of food, such as where he squeezed them for the sake of the bread.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג דכ"ע משקה הבא לאוכל לאו אוכל הוא - אלא משקה הוא, והיינו טעמא דמ"ד לא הוכשר, שמתחילה נסחט אדעתא דאזיל לאיבוד, שהאור שואבו ושורפו:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:1.english: This is the text [we read]: Everyone agrees that liquid that comes into food is not food - rather, it is a liquid; and this is the reason of the one who says [it] was not rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity]: because from the outset it was squeezed out with the intention that it go to waste, for the fire draws it out and burns it.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:2.hebrew: המפצע בזיתים - בלציי"ר, כדי שיהיו רכין:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:2.english: One who crushes olives - Blecier [in Old French, meaning to bruise or crush them] so that they become soft.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:3.hebrew: הוכשר - דניחא ליה במשחא דטייף עלייהו, שמתוך כך הם מרבים טעם:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:3.english: [It] is rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity] - For he is pleased with the oil that floats upon them, as through this they increase [in] flavor.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:4.hebrew: לסופתן במלח - שמתוך שהן קשין, אין המלח נדבק בהן, ומפצעם לרככן מבחוץ מעט:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:4.english: To dip them in salt - For since they are hard, the salt does not adhere to them, and he cracks them to soften them slightly on the outside.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:3:5.english: [It] is not rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity] - For he does not intend for their liquid to be extracted.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:4:1.hebrew: לידע אם הגיעו זיתיו למסוק - צריך הוא לראות אם שומנו נוח לצאת, מיהו המשקה אזיל לאיבוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:4:1.english: To know whether his olives have reached [the stage] to be harvested - he needs to see whether its oil comes out easily; however, the liquid goes to waste.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:5:1.hebrew: הני תנאי - דמפצע, ודאי במשקה העומד לאיבוד פליגי, כדאמרי'. אבל תנאי דמחליק, לאו בעומד לאיבוד פליגי, דלאו לאיבוד אזל, שהרי לצחצח האוכל נתנו, והרי מצחצחו. אלא במשקה העומד לצחצחו לאוכל קא מיפלגי, דא"נ משקה הבא לאוכל משקה הוא, ה"מ היכא דקא שריף ליה, א"נ שטר ביה ריפתא, דתורת משקה עביד; אבל לצחצחו פליגי:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:5:1.english: These tanna’im - [That is, the tanna’im] of one who crushes [olives] certainly disagree regarding liquid that stands [to go] to waste, as we said. However, the tanna’im of one who smooths [food] do not disagree regarding [liquid] that stands [to go] to waste, for it does not go to waste, since he placed it to shine the food, and behold, it shines it. Rather, they disagree regarding liquid that stands to shine the food, for even if liquid that comes for food is [considered] a liquid, this applies [only] where he sips it, or else dips bread in it, where it serves the function of a liquid; but [where it is used] to shine it, they disagree.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:6:1.hebrew: ודג לצירו - סחיטת דג להוציא צירו, לאו משקה הוא אלא אוכלין:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:6:1.english: And [squeezing] a fish for its brine - Squeezing a fish to extract its brine is not [considered] a liquid, rather food.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:7:1.english: Pickled vegetables - Raw vegetables pickled in wine and vinegar.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:7:2.hebrew: לגופו - אם לאכול הכבשים סוחטן ממשקה הצף עליהן והנבלע בהן, מותר לכתחילה, דלא מפרק הוא, הואיל ולאו למשקה הוא צריך:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:7:2.english: For itself - If [it is] to eat the pickled vegetables [that] he squeezes them from the liquid floating on them and absorbed in them, it is permitted ab initio, for it is not [considered] extracting [liquid], since he does not need the liquid:

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:7:3.hebrew: פטור - שאין זה מפרק, שאין המשקה הזה יוצא מן הכבשים, שלא גדל בתוכן; אבל אסור אטו זיתים וענבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:7:3.english: He is exempt - Because this is not [the forbidden labor of] extracting (mefarek), for this liquid does not come out of the pickled vegetables [themselves], as it did not grow inside them; however, it is prohibited on account of olives and grapes.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:8:1.hebrew: שלקות - אפילו למימיהן, לאו משקה נינהו אלא אוכל:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:8:1.english: Boiled vegetables - Even [when squeezed] for their liquids, [they] are not [considered] a beverage, but rather food.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:8:2.hebrew: למימיהן פטור אבל אסור - והא שלקות דומיא דדג לצירן הוא, ולא שרי ליה שמואל לכתחילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 145a:8:2.english: For their liquids, he is exempt, but it is prohibited - Yet boiled [items] are similar to fish [pressed] for their brine, and Shmuel did not permit it ab initio.

Rashi on Shabbat 145a:9:1.english: My eyes have seen, and not a stranger - This [matter] that I wish to tell you — that it was stated in the name of Rav.

Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:10:1.hebrew: כבשים שסחטן לגופן מותר למימיהן פטור אבל אסור - רב לטעמיה, דאמר לקמן: דבר תורה אינו חייב אלא על דריכת זיתים וענבים. ולפירוש הקונטרס דפי' משום דאתי המשקה מעלמא, קשה לרבי: אמאי גזרו להדוקי אודרא אפומא דשישא בשלהי תולין (לעיל שבת דף קמא.) שמא יסחוט? הא אפילו סחיט, ליכא איסור דאורייתא! מיהו י"ל דהתם רבא דקאמר לה, וס"ל כר' יוחנן דמחייב חטאת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:10:1.english: "Pickled vegetables that one squeezed: for themselves, it is permitted; for their liquids, he is exempt, but it is prohibited" - Rav [is consistent] with his own reasoning, as he says later [that] by Torah law one is liable only for treading olives and grapes. And according to the explanation of Rashi, who explained [that the reason for this is] because the liquid comes from elsewhere, it is difficult for the Rabbi: Why did they decree against stuffing a wad [of cloth] into the mouth of a flask at the end of [the chapter] Tolin (above, Shabbat 141a) lest one squeeze [it]? Even if he squeezes [it], there is no Torah prohibition! However, one can say that there it is Rava who says it, and he holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan, who holds one liable for a sin-offering.

Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:10:2.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן אמר אחד כבשין ואחד שלקות לגופן מותר למימיהן חייב חטאת - ובדג לצירו נמי הוה מחייב ר' יוחנן חטאת לתוך הקערה, דדג לצירו מדמינן לשלקות בכולה שמעתיה, דפריך מדשמואל דשלקות אההיא דדג לצירו. ופי' ר' דהלכה כר' יוחנן, דקיי"ל כוותיה לגבי רב ושמואל. ושמעינן ממילתא דר"י שאסור לסחוט כבשים ושלקות למימיהן, ואם סחט — חייב חטאת; ולא הפריש בסחיטה בין קדירה לקער', אלא הכל אסור. מתוך אלו דברים מתברר שאין הלכה לא כשמואל ולא כרב, שאמרו: סוחט אדם אשכול של ענבים לתוך הקדירה. ויש שמעמידין דברי רב ושמואל ביו"ט, מדדייק רב חסדא מדברי שמואל כן; ואין לנו להדורי אפריכי ולאפוקי שמעתא מדוכתיה, אלא ודאי בשבת קאמרי רב ושמואל, ואין הלכה כמותן לא בשבת ולא ביו"ט. ע"כ פי' ר"ח. ומה שדקדק, מדלא מפליג ר' יוחנן משמע דמיירי אפילו לתוך הקדירה — אין זה דיוק; דהא רב ושמואל נמי אסרי סתמא בכבשים למימיהן, ואע"ג דשרו לסחוט בהדיא אשכול של ענבים לתוך הקדירה. ומה שדחה דברי המעמידין דברי רב ושמואל ביו"ט — אומר ר"ת שהדין עמו, אבל דברי רב חסדא ביום טוב כדפירשתי לעיל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:10:2.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: [With regard to] both pickled vegetables and boiled vegetables, [squeezing them] for themselves is permitted; for their liquids, one is liable to [bring] a sin-offering - And with regard to fish [pressed] for its brine into a bowl, Rabbi Yoḥanan would also hold [one] liable to [bring] a sin-offering, for throughout the entire discussion we compare fish [pressed] for its brine to boiled vegetables, as [the Gemara] raises a difficulty from Shmuel's [ruling] regarding boiled vegetables against that [statement] regarding fish [pressed] for its brine. And our Rabbi [Rabbeinu Ḥananel] explained that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, since we hold in accordance with him against Rav and Shmuel. And we learn from the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan that it is prohibited to squeeze pickled vegetables and boiled vegetables for their liquids, and if one squeezed [them] he is liable to [bring] a sin-offering; and he did not distinguish in [the prohibition of] squeezing between [squeezing into] a pot and [into] a bowl, rather everything is prohibited. From these words it becomes clear that the halakha is neither in accordance with Shmuel nor in accordance with Rav, who said: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot. And there are those who establish the words of Rav and Shmuel as referring to a Festival, from the fact that Rav Ḥisda infers this from the words of Shmuel; however, we should not go looking for forced explanations and remove the discussion from its plain context, rather Rav and Shmuel certainly spoke regarding Shabbat, and the halakha is not in accordance with them, neither on Shabbat nor on a Festival. Thus far is the commentary of Rabbeinu Ḥananel. And [as for] that which he inferred — [namely,] that since Rabbi Yoḥanan does not distinguish, it implies that he is speaking even [of squeezing] into a pot — this is not a valid inference; for Rav and Shmuel also prohibit [squeezing] pickled vegetables for their liquids without qualification, even though they explicitly permit squeezing a cluster of grapes into a pot. And [as for] that which he rejected the words of those who establish the words of Rav and Shmuel as referring to a Festival — Rabbeinu Tam says that he is right, but the words of Rav Ḥisda [do refer] to a Festival, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:1:1.hebrew: כביצה מכוונת טהור - פי' בקונטרס שאע"פ שהאוכל טמא, אינו מטמא את המשקה, שאין אוכל מטמא בפחות מכביצה. והאי טעמא לא ניחא אלא למ"ד בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף לג: ושם) משקים מיפקד פקידי, אבל למ"ד התם מיבלע בליעי, טמאים המשקין מאליהן כיון שנגע באוכל, [ומשני התם דבמתני' מיירי בענבים שלא הוכשרו — לאימת מתכשרי? לכי סחיט להו, וכי סחיט להו בציר שעוריה; והשתא לפי' רש"י, מה בכך?] מיד כשיצאה הטיפה ראשונה נטמאה, הואיל ואוכל מקבל טומאה בכל שהוא. ומה שהקשה ר"ת לפירו', פי' לעיל בריש המצניע (שבת דף צא.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:1:1.english: [In] the exact amount of an egg-bulk, it is pure - Rashi explained that even though the food is impure, it does not render the liquid impure, because food does not transmit impurity [when it is] less than an egg-bulk. However, this reason is only satisfactory according to the one who says in Chapter Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 33b, and there [in the parallel discussion]) that liquids [absorbed in food] are "deposited" [separately inside the food]; but according to the one who says there that they are "absorbed" [as part of the food], the liquids are impure on their own once [the impure person] touched the food — (and there [in Pesachim] it answers that the Mishnah speaks of grapes that had not been rendered susceptible [to impurity] — when are they rendered susceptible? When he squeezes them, and when he squeezes them, their measure is reduced [below an egg-bulk]; and now, according to Rashi's explanation, what of it?) — immediately when the first drop emerges, it is impure, since food contracts impurity in any amount [even less than an egg-bulk]. And that which Rabbeinu Tam objected to his explanation, we explained above at the beginning of [Chapter] HaMatzni'a (Shabbat 91a):

Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:3:1.hebrew: דכ"ע משקה הבא לאוכל לאו אוכל הוא - לא מצינן למימר דכ"ע אוכל הוא, א"כ מ"ט דמ"ד הוכשר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:3:1.english: "Everyone agrees that liquid that comes into food is not food" - We cannot say that everyone agrees it is food, [for] if so, what is the reason of the one who says it is rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity]?

Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:4:1.hebrew: אם הגיעו זיתיו למסוק כו' - מה שקשה ליה לרב נחמן, דמפרש בפ"ק (דף יז.) דגזרו לבצור בטהרה משום דפעמים שאדם הולך כו'. שם פירשתי בד"ה גוזרני:
Tosafot on Shabbat 145a:4:1.english: "Whether his olives have reached [the stage] to be harvested," etc. - [Regarding] that which is difficult for Rav Nachman, who explains in the first chapter (17a) that they decreed to harvest [grapes] in purity because sometimes a person goes, etc. — I explained [this] there, s.v. Gozrani.
